newsitem.title: USA: Figgie sets Scott Aviation acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Figgie sets Scott Aviation acquisitions.

text.p: Figgie International Inc said Monday it would use the proceeds for the sale of its Snorkel division to launch an aggressive growth strategy -- principally acquisitions for its Scott Aviation unit.

Figgie also said that in light of the decision to sell the Snorkel division, a manufacturer of self-propelled aerial work platforms, to Omniquip International Inc, the Figgie board has decided to delay naming a new chief executive officer until the end of August.
"We already have identified and evaluated several acquisition candidates," said Glen Lindemann, Scott president.

"We are particularly looking at companies and product lines that serve respiratory and related markets. Acquisitions should increase our existing market share and offer significant growth opportunities -- both through international expansion and new product lines."

According to Lindemann, Scott plans to undertake a significant acquisition in the third quarter. The division is seeking to leverage the Scott brand name, its distribution network, and core technologies, he added.
Commenting on the decision to delay naming a new CEO, Chairman John Reilly said, "Figgie is a different company today.
"Before making our final decision, we want to re-evaluate each candidate to ensure that we choose a corporate leader whose skills match the future needs of this company."
He said the delay was simply a final review of the candidates and not the beginning of a new search process.

Figgie said the sale of Snorkel to Omniquip for $150 million cash plus the assumption of certain liabilities is subject to regulatory approval and certain closing conditions. The parties expect the sale to be completed within 45 days.

Chief Financial Officer Steven Siemborski said the sale is not related to the unsolicited acquisition proposal for Figgie made by Chicago-based, privately-owned Heico Holding on July 3. "Negotiations with Omniquip began long before we received Heico's proposal," said Siemborski.
